Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajesh Shankar For the Petitioners : Mr. Navin Kumar
Singh, Advocate For the Resp.-State : Mr. J.F. Toppo, G.A.-V Mr. A.R. Kisku, A.C. to G.A.-V For the
Resp.-NHAI : Mrs. Sweety Topno, Advocate Order No. 08 Dated: 20.04.2023

The present writ petition has been filed for the following reliefs:
(i) For quashing the order dated 15.01.2018 (Anneuxre-9 to the writ petition) passed by the respondent no. 3- the Additional Collector, Bokaro-cum-Arbitrator under the National Highways Act, 1956 (in short, "the Act, 1956") in Land Acquisition Appeal No. 41 of 2017 whereby the appeal preferred by the petitioners seeking enhancement of compensation of the awarded amount in lieu of acquisition of land in question for widening of NH-23 has been rejected.
(ii) For quashing the report of seven-members committee, constituted by the Deputy Commissioner, Bokaro (the respondent no. 2), annexed with letter no. 1388 dated 22.12.2017 (Annexure-8 to the writ petition) issued by the District Land Acquisition Officer, Bokaro to the respondent no. 3.
(iii) For issuance of direction upon the respondents to make payment of compensation to the petitioner for acquisition of the land in question @ Rs.77,562/- per decimal.

sentences.text: 2. So far as the prayer no. (ii) with respect to quashing the report of seven-members committee is concerned
, learned counsel for the petitioner does not press the same.

3. Mr. A.R. Kisku and Mrs. Sweety Topno, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent-State of Jharkhand and the respondent-NHAI respectively, jointly raise a preliminary objection with regard to maintainability of the present writ petition on the ground that the petitioner has got alternative/statutory/efficacious remedy under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (in short, "the Act, 1996") against the order dated 15.01.2018 passed by the respondent no. 3 in Land Acquisition Appeal No. 41 of 2017.

4. Since the respondents have raised an issue of maintainability of the present writ petition, it would be appropriate to deal with the said issue at the first instance.
5. Section 3-G(6) of the Act, 1956 clearly provides that the provisions of the Act, 1996 shall apply to every arbitration under the said Act, subject to the other provisions of the same.

Thus, the impugned order dated 15.01.2018 passed by the respondent No.3 in Land Acquisition Appeal No. 41 of 2017 has to be treated as an award passed within the meaning and the provisions of the Act, 1996.
The Act, 1956 does not provide any further Forum for challenging the award passed by an arbitrator under Section 3-G(5) of the said Act.

Thus, if any person is aggrieved with the award of an arbitrator passed under Section 3-G(5) of the Act, 1956, he has got the remedy to file an application under Section 34 of the Act, 1996 for setting aside the same.

6. Hence, this Court is of the view that the petitioner has got alternative/statutory/efficacious remedy of filing an application before the appropriate Court seeking challenge to the order/award dated 15.01.2018 passed by the respondent No.3 in Land Acquisition Appeal No. 41 of 2017.
7. The present writ petition is accordingly dismissed as not maintainable.

8. The petitioners are however at liberty to take alternative/ statutory/efficacious recourse under Section 34 of the Act, 1996 against the impugned order/award dated 15.01.2018 passed by the respondent No.3 in Land Acquisition Appeal No. 41 of 2017 taking all possible grounds as available under law.

(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Ritesh/
